document.title: Working Interfaces — Architecture Concept
document.purpose: Capture the current reduced architecture direction for rapid prototyping and later product development.
document.important_note: This is a clean rewrite. It replaces the earlier architecture concept rather than extending it.
document.decision_rule: Nothing becomes a fixed architectural rule until a real prototype or product workflow proves it.

project_definition.name: Working Interfaces
project_definition.working_description: A knowledge-first design and prototyping environment for serious, information-rich interfaces.

core_principles: Keep the speed and visibility of plain HTML.
Use TypeScript only where validation, durability, or product confidence matters.
Build one source of knowledge that can later feed multiple surfaces.
Do not create packages or services before they have a real consumer.
Keep framework-independent knowledge independent from applications.
Prefer domain language over generic SaaS structure.

phase_one_goal.name: Knowledge Loop
phase_one_goal.objective: Prove that one canonical record can feed both human and machine-readable surfaces without reducing prototyping speed.
proof: Validated with a small Zod schema
success_criteria: Raw HTML experiments stay directly accessible.
The generated site is still inspectable HTML.
No advanced service architecture is required.
The result teaches us whether canonical records are useful.

field-manual.purpose: Human-facing publishing shell, navigation, record pages, and experiment index.

raw-html.purpose: Fast, unrestricted visual and interaction prototypes.
rules: A prototype may remain only as visual evidence.

tokens.purpose: Only add when shared semantic tokens are actually used.

tools: YAML or JSON for structured overlays
flow: Create or change an idea in raw HTML.
When the idea survives, write a short canonical record.
Render the record in the field manual.
Generate JSON from the same source.

Astro.role: Field-manual publishing shell and typed content consumer.
Astro.constraint: Astro must not become the framework core.

TypeScript.role: Validation, build logic, and later durable product code.
TypeScript.rule: Use simple TypeScript; avoid clever type architecture.

Zod.role: Small validation layer for record metadata.

React.reason: The product framework should be validated by an actual workflow rather than selected only from theory.
React.current_hypothesis: React + Vite + TypeScript remains a strong candidate.

Lit.reason: Portability is not yet a real requirement.
Lit.trigger: A proven component must genuinely run in at least two host frameworks.

database.reason: Real access patterns, provenance queries, append-only history, and operational needs are not yet known.
database.hard_rule: Future domain logic should remain storage-independent.

MCP.trigger: Manual context bundles have proven useful and a real client needs MCP.
MCP.rule: MCP must not influence the canonical knowledge model.

HTTP_API.trigger: A second real consumer requires programmatic access.

adoption_lane.purpose: Express stricter vocabulary, process constraints, and visual defaults without changing the general core.

milestones.name: Clean repository
milestones.output: New Working Interfaces repository with current manual imported.

milestones.name: Prototype lane
milestones.output: Raw HTML experiments remain directly usable and indexed.

milestones.name: Astro shell
milestones.output: Homepage, shared navigation, experiment index, and one documentation layout.

milestones.name: One-source proof
milestones.output: One Markdown record rendered as HTML, JSON, and raw Markdown.

milestones.name: Minimal validation
milestones.output: Small Zod schema validating essential record metadata.

milestones.name: Second linked record
milestones.output: One pattern record related to the first component record.

later_product_hypothesis.organization_rule: Feature-first structure using domain folders rather than generic technical folders.

future_context_work.first_step: Create one manual downloadable context bundle.
future_context_work.goal: Test whether focused canonical knowledge improves LLM output.

risks.response: Keep raw HTML as a permanent first-class lane.
Knowledge files and schemas remain usable without Astro.
Create packages only when a real consumer exists.

risks.risk: Technology decisions are made before product evidence.
risks.response: Defer React, Lit, database, API, and MCP decisions until concrete triggers appear.

risks.risk: Canonical knowledge becomes cumbersome to author.
risks.response: Start with direct Markdown and minimal validation; no CMS.

open_questions: Does the one-record HTML/JSON/Markdown loop feel fast enough in daily use?
Should knowledge live at repository root or inside a package after phase one?
Is Markdown frontmatter sufficient for component and pattern records?
Does Adoption Lane work as a recipe overlay without a runtime engine?
Which real workflow should validate the future product stack?
When does a second consumer justify an API?
When does repeated manual bundle creation justify a Context Builder?
mantra: Add TypeScript only where confidence matters.
